git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(io): seven path builtins failed in SILENCE, and two more named the wrong one

Sixteen failing path calls in one program. `php -n` 8.5.6 prints SIXTEEN warnings.
elephc printed nine — and two of those named a function the program never called:

    unlink  rmdir  rename  mkdir  opendir  touch  chmod   → nothing at all
    readfile  file                                        → "file_get_contents(…)"

A script that checked the return value behaved the same either way. A script that
read the log learned nothing about why anything failed.

THE SHAPES ARE NOT ONE SHAPE, which is why `__rt_path_op_warning` takes its text in
two pieces rather than assuming `name(path): reason`:

    Warning: unlink(nope.txt): No such file or directory
    Warning: rmdir(f.txt): Not a directory
    Warning: opendir(nope): Failed to open directory: No such file or directory
    Warning: rename(nope.txt,other.txt): No such file or directory
    Warning: mkdir(): File exists
    Warning: chmod(): No such file or directory
    Warning: touch(): Unable to create file /no/such/x.txt because No such file …

`mkdir()` and `chmod()` name no path AT ALL — the parentheses stay empty though a
path was passed — and `touch()` puts it mid-sentence. `rename()` names both, comma
and no space, which is the one shape that needed a helper of its own.

The two mis-named ones read through `file_get_contents`, and left to itself that
helper names ITSELF. The mechanism to say otherwise already existed for `copy()`;
`readfile()` and `file()` now publish their names through it too.

A `file://` URL changes what php prints, and in two different directions. The
stream-open family names the URL the PROGRAM wrote — `file_get_contents(file:///no/
such)`, not the path it was reduced to — so `__rt_path_cstr` now keeps the whole
argument in the buffer and publishes its base, which `__rt_path_diag_name` spends
once. The metadata family does the opposite: it names the stripped path, and for
`touch()` and `chmod()` a URL takes the WRAPPER HOOK's shape, which puts the path
in the parentheses (twice, for `touch()`) and words `chmod()`'s failure as
`Operation failed:`. All measured, all pinned.

The two entry points of the composer carry their own copy of the body rather than
sharing one behind a flag: a `label_global` opens an ATOM on macOS, and the shared
local label was a cross-atom reference `-dead_strip` removes. The emitter's own
gate caught it by name.

Verified: a 37-program differential sweep of the streams surface is 37/37 identical
with 0 refusals, the 183-program round-8 corpus is unchanged at 180, and 1097
`io::`, 272 `spl::` and 1535 unit tests pass. x86_64 mirrors every site and
assembles clean; the CI x86 shard remains its execution oracle.

Found and left open: `chown($p, fileowner($p))` is refused at compile time —
`fileowner()` is declared `int|false` and the check takes only a bare `Int` or
`Str`. Relaxing the check ALONE is a false win: the argument then arrives
string-converted and the call answers `false` in silence, which is worse than the
refusal. It needs the argument boundary fixed, not the check.
